tasks.short: Turn the Finance Director's budget guidelines into cost-centre rules, templates and deadlines for site and department managers.

today.trigger: Annual budget kick-off in September, plus mid-year directives from the Finance Director or the board (hiring freeze, flex cap, cost cuts).
steps: Read the directive memo and the board or MT minutes behind it
Translate it into rules per cost centre: headcount caps, flex-hour limits, CAO wage increase assumptions, capex thresholds
Update the Excel budget templates and the guidance note on SharePoint
Email managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo and answer their questions
Check submissions against the rules and chase deviations
drudgery: Rewriting the same guidance note in three versions for the three sites
Answering the same manager questions by mail over and over
Checking each template by hand for rule breaches
today.time_sinks: Clarifying ambiguous directives with the Finance Director and handling manager questions and non-compliant submissions.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts the guidance note, the rule table and an FAQ from the directive memo and last year's version; the analyst edits instead of writing from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: When a manager submits a budget file, rule checks run automatically (flex share, headcount cap, CAO increase applied) and return a deviation list the same day.
lenses.ambitious: Every directive gets a one-page impact sheet per cost centre showing what it means in euros and FTE, so managers argue about numbers rather than wording.
lenses.joy: No more copy-pasting the guidance note per site or answering the same question twenty times; the analyst spends time on the hard judgement calls with the Finance Director.
lenses.options: For a directive like 'reduce flex cost 10%', generate three implementation variants (cap per site, cap per peak season, shift to own staff) with their cost and service effects.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains a written budget rulebook and the check logic, and reviews where rules are being gamed, instead of policing each submission.
reach: Controller: first-line review of budget submissions against policy
HR Business Partner: headcount and flex planning rules aligned with workforce plans

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what an ambiguous directive actually means, negotiating exceptions with site managers, and knowing which rules the works council or CAO make sensitive.
tasks.pattern_why: The interpretation and policy choice stay with the analyst and Finance Director; AI drafts text and rule tables, and deterministic checks validate submissions.

in_practice.trigger: Finance Director publishes a budget directive or the annual budget cycle opens.
steps: Analyst uploads the directive and last year's guidance to a Copilot/Claude workspace
AI drafts the guidance note, rule table and FAQ per site
Analyst edits and the Finance Director approves
Rules are encoded as Excel or Power Query checks on submitted templates
Deviation reports go back to managers automatically
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director signs off the guidance note and rule table before release to managers.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder with versioned guidance and a deviation log per cost centre

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts documents in Word from source files on SharePoint.
Rule checks on structured Excel budget templates can be built in Power Query without a model.
LLM drafts of policy guidance cut writing time for analysts by a third or more.

risks: AI-drafted guidance states a rule the Finance Director did not intend
Managers treat automated deviation lists as final and stop discussing context
Headcount rules touching staff may require works council (OR) consultation that a draft omits
research_questions: How many hours per cycle go to writing guidance versus answering questions versus checking submissions?
Are budget templates structured enough for rule checks, or does each site modify them?
Which directives in the last two years needed OR involvement or CAO checks?

tasks.short: Build business cases comparing options, like own staff versus agency flex workers, new forklifts, or lease versus buy.

today.trigger: A manager or the Finance Director asks for a business case: a capex request, a new customer contract, a lease proposal, flex versus own staff.
steps: Collect cost data from AFAS, agency invoices and the requester's quotes
Build an Excel model with NPV, payback and sensitivity
Check assumptions with the requester and operations
Write a short memo or slide deck with a recommendation
Present to the Finance Director or MT
drudgery: Rebuilding a model structure that already exists in an older file
Pulling and cleaning agency invoice and hour data by hand
today.time_sinks: Data collection from several systems and chasing requesters for assumptions.

lenses.faster: A standard business-case template with pre-loaded AFAS and agency cost data means the analyst fills in assumptions instead of building the model; an LLM drafts the memo from the model output.
lenses.autonomous: Capex and lease requests submitted via a form get a first-pass case automatically: cost data pulled, standard NPV and payback calculated, missing inputs flagged to the requester.
lenses.ambitious: Every capex request above a threshold gets a proper case with sensitivity, and the company does a post-investment review a year later for the first time.
lenses.joy: Gone is the data hunting and slide formatting; left is challenging assumptions and finding the option nobody proposed.
lenses.options: Each case shows three to five alternatives (buy, lease, rent, agency, own staff, defer) with sensitivity on volume and wage increases, not just the requester's preferred one.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the case template, the cost drivers library and the post-investment review, and checks auto-generated cases rather than building each one.
reach: Controller: capex approval review and post-investment audits
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: cost of own staff versus flex under the CAO
Credit and Collections Officer: customer profitability inputs for new contracts

tasks.human_edge: Judging which assumptions are realistic, knowing the operational context of a site, and the recommendation that the Finance Director will defend.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across systems (AFAS, agency portals, quotes) with exceptions, producing a case that only counts once the analyst checks and signs it.

in_practice.trigger: A business-case request form is submitted on SharePoint or Teams.
steps: Agent reads the request and attached quotes
Agent pulls relevant costs from the AFAS extract and agency invoice data
Agent fills the standard Excel case model and runs sensitivity
Agent drafts a two-page memo with options and flags weak assumptions
Analyst reviews, adjusts and sends to the Finance Director
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves model and memo before anything goes to the Finance Director or MT.
data_needed: Cost of capital set by Finance Director
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint business-case register with model version, assumptions and decision

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel can generate formulas and analyses on tabular data.
LLM agents can fill a fixed financial template from structured extracts and draft a memo.
Standardised business-case templates shorten preparation time in finance teams.

risks: Formula or data errors in an auto-built model that look plausible
Agency rate data incomplete because invoices arrive as PDFs in different formats
Requesters game the form to get a favourable first-pass result
research_questions: How many business cases were made last year and how long did each take?
Is agency hour and invoice data available in a structured form from all three agencies?
Would the Finance Director accept a standard template for all capex above a set threshold?
How often did a case change after assumptions were challenged?

tasks.short: Look for ways to cut costs and raise margin, like flex use, overtime, warehouse productivity, customer pricing.

today.trigger: Monthly results review, a margin dip at a site, or an MT request for savings.
steps: Scan Power BI dashboards and AFAS actuals for variances
Dig into drivers: overtime, agency hours, absence, fuel, customer margins
Talk to site managers to understand causes
Write up opportunities with estimated savings
Track whether agreed actions happen
drudgery: Manually slicing the same dashboards each month to spot outliers
Merging agency hours with AFAS hours in Excel
today.time_sinks: Finding the signal in variance data and reconciling data from different sources before any analysis can start.

lenses.faster: Automated variance and driver analysis on the nightly AFAS extract surfaces the top outliers with a written explanation, so the analyst starts with a shortlist.
lenses.autonomous: After each nightly refresh, rules flag anomalies (agency hours above plan, overtime spikes, customer margin below floor) and post them to a Finance Teams channel.
lenses.ambitious: A standing savings pipeline with owners, euro values and progress, reviewed monthly by the MT, instead of ad hoc ideas that fade.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet merging and dashboard trawling; more time on the floor in Venlo or Tilburg understanding why the numbers move.
lenses.options: For each outlier, AI proposes several levers (rostering change, agency renegotiation, pricing clause, process change) with rough savings, for the analyst to test.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the anomaly rules and driver model and runs the savings pipeline, rather than hunting for each opportunity by hand.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: overtime and absence drivers
Credit and Collections Officer: customer profitability and payment terms

tasks.human_edge: Understanding operations on site, judging which ideas are feasible given CAO and works council constraints, and persuading managers to act.
tasks.pattern_why: Anomaly detection is deterministic and an LLM can explain drivers, but choosing and selling improvements stays with the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly Power BI refresh and the monthly close.
steps: Deterministic rules on the AFAS extract flag cost and margin anomalies per site and customer
LLM writes a short driver explanation for each flag
Analyst picks the ones worth pursuing and talks to site managers
Opportunities go into a savings tracker with owner and value
Monthly MT summary drafted by AI, reviewed by analyst
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst decides which opportunities to raise; MT decides which to act on.
data_needed: AFAS GL, hours and absence extract
Budget and forecast per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint savings tracker with source anomaly, owner, estimated and realised savings

evidence.claim: Power BI has built-in anomaly detection on line charts and smart narrative summaries.
LLMs can write variance explanations from structured driver data.
Combining agency and payroll hours exposes flex cost savings in warehousing.

risks: Too many false-positive flags and the channel gets ignored
Analysis at individual employee level (overtime, absence) touches AVG/GDPR and may need OR agreement
Savings estimates by AI overstated and erode trust with the MT
research_questions: Can agency hours be matched to AFAS cost centres reliably today?
How many savings ideas from last year were implemented and what did they deliver?
Which anomaly rules would site managers find useful rather than noise?

role.altitude: From building each analysis and policing each budget to owning the budget rulebook, business-case template, driver model and savings pipeline that run largely on their own, and checking their output.
reach: Controller: budget submission review, capex approval and post-investment review
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: workforce cost and flex drivers
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: CAO cost modelling
Credit and Collections Officer: customer profitability analysis
role.ceiling_note: About 30 to 45 percent of the time on these tasks can go; the limit is data quality (agency invoices, cost-centre mapping), the judgement and persuasion needed with site managers and the Finance Director, and OR and AVG constraints on people-level analysis.
skills_to_grow: Power Query and data modelling on the AFAS extract
Writing and testing rules and prompts for automated checks and drafts
Facilitating decisions with site managers and the MT
role.ambitious_version: The two analysts run a driver-based planning system where every directive, business case and savings idea is quantified per site within a day, forecasts are rolled monthly with scenarios, and the MT reviews a live savings pipeline, which supports a faster close with a forecast the business trusts.
